title: Nineteen Dutch windmills were built to drain low land
body: At Kinderdijk, windmills helped lift excess water out of low-lying areas called polders. The World Heritage site preserves 19 drainage mills alongside the channels, embankments and sluices that helped move water on.
takeaway: The mills were only one link in a system that had to carry the lifted water away.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Mill Network at Kinderdijk-Elshout (1997)
visual: a line of windmills beside a still drainage canal

title: The Brooklyn Bridge's piers were built over pressurised chambers
body: Before the Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883, workers excavated below the river in chambers called caissons. Compressed air kept water outside while the chamber and the pier above it sank as material was removed.
takeaway: Building a pier may require making a temporary dry workplace below the waterline.
source: American Society of Civil Engineers, Brooklyn Bridge
visual: a cutaway view of a bridge pier under construction above a chamber in the riverbed

title: Sanaa has tower houses built in part from compacted earth
body: Yemen's old city of Sanaa lies in a mountain valley about 2,200 metres above sea level. Its tall, multi-storey houses include examples built with rammed earth, a material made by compacting soil in layers.
takeaway: The height a material can reach depends on how it is formed and supported.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old City of Sanaa (1986)
visual: tall earthen houses with pale decorative window surrounds in old Sanaa

title: Korea's Seokguram Grotto was assembled from granite blocks
body: The eighth-century Buddhist grotto on Mount Toham is an artificial cave. Builders used granite to create an entrance chamber, a passage and a circular room containing a large Buddha statue.
takeaway: Cave-like spaces can be designed by assembling stone as well as by removing it.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
visual: a stone Buddha inside a round chamber lined with granite blocks
